rationale: R5 reference classes are DECLARED by evaluating `setRefClass("Name", ...)`; the assignment is a convenience binding, not the declaration. The corpus proves it — r-Rcpp/R/00_classes.R:27,37,58 declare `C++Field`, `C++OverloadedMethods` and `C++Constructor` as bare file-level statements — and the analyzer read only the assignment spelling, so every statement-form class, its fields and its `contains=` relation were invisible. THE FIRE HALF pins the statement form on BOTH class-carrying surfaces (bare and `methods::`-qualified) plus its `fields=` members and its `contains=` edges. THE DEDUPE HALF is the reason the counts are EXACT rather than `>= 1`: adding a statement path while the assignment path also runs would publish each assigned class twice (symbol twice, `contains` edge twice), and a presence-only pin cannot see a duplicate — the first version of this fix DID double-publish, because tree-sitter hands out a fresh JS wrapper per node access and the `===` guard silently failed; the fix is `sameNode`, and these counts are what make a regression to `===` go red. THE NEGATIVE HALF: `factory <- function(Class) setRefClass(Class, ...)` computes the class name at RUNTIME, so no symbol or edge may be invented for it — a fabricated `Class` declaration is worse than a missing one. `BareChild`/`BareComposed` also pin the composition split (single base -> extends, list -> mixes_in) on the statement spelling.
